newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: CIVIL LIBERTIES CRITICISE BAN ON HANSON

The Queensland Civil Liberties Council says Ipswich City Council, west of Brisbane, could be setting a dangerous precedent in deciding to ban Pauline Hanson's One Nation party from all council owned and operated buildings.
Ipswich Councillor, Paul Tully, says the decision of the Labor controlled council was influenced by a violent protest at the One Nation launch at the Ipswich Civic Hall in April.
He says the ban comes into effect immediately, and forces One Nation supporters to cancel tomorrow night's planned party meeting at the Ipswich humanities centre.
Civil Liberties President Ian Dearden says the council can't justify its decision by saying ratepayers should not have to pay for security at such meetings.
MINISTERS OFF OVERSEAS AS JOHN HOWARD RECUPERATES
Seven Federal Government Ministers are heading to Japan for top level government talks.
Treasurer Peter Costello is again Acting Prime Minister, while John Howard shows signs of recovery from pneumonia.
Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer flew out last night to head the Australian delegation to the annual ministerial council meeting with Japan - Australia's biggest trade partner.
He will join six other ministers, including Foreign Minister Alexander Downer and Environment Minister Robert Hill.
Trade issues will dominate the talks, with hopes of boosting Australian access to Japan's highly protected agricultural markets.
TREASURER'S GOLD COMMENTS CRITICISED
The Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has been attacked for making what it is claimed are damaging and inaccurate comments about the international gold scene.

George Milling-Stanley of the World Gold Council has told the annual "Diggers and Dealers" forum in Kalgoorlie, in Western Australia, that the Treasurer's remarks in defence of the Reserve Bank's gold sell-off did more harm than the actual transaction.
He says it was incorrect for Mr Costello to say that gold no longer plays a significant role in the international financial system.
SURVEY FINDS ANGLICANS THE MOST TOLERANT
A survey of Australian churchgoers' attitudes towards sex and sexuality has found that Anglicans are the most tolerant denomination.
The National Church Life Survey questioned about 300,000 churchgoers from 23 different denominations.
It found Anglicans the most accepting of homosexuals in their congregations and 35 per cent of Anglicans would accept gay church leaders.
The Anglican Archbishop of Perth, Peter Carnley, says different outlooks on life are very much a part of the Anglican Church.
